dedupe_keys.name: wpdx water point data exchange global rural water point repository wpdx basic and wpdx

description: The Water Point Data Exchange is a global repository of rural water point records (wells, springs, boreholes, tapstands and small schemes) shared by governments, NGOs and researchers and harmonised to the WPdx Data Standard, with coordinates, water source and technology, installation and rehabilitation year, management, payment, water quality and whether water was present when last assessed. It is an initiative of the Global Water Challenge, governed by a working group of sector organisations. On 2026-09-26 WPdx-Basic, which holds every shared record after validation, had 838,209 rows from 60 countries, and WPdx+, a cleaned and enhanced subset for countries with good administrative matching, had 440,270 rows with 74 fields including distances to roads and towns; both were updated that day. Coverage is global in principle but mostly sub-Saharan Africa, with parts of Asia and Latin America. Both datasets are free to filter and download, with an API, and per-country extracts are on HDX under CC BY-SA. Caveats: records come from many surveys of different dates, a status is only as recent as the last report, and coverage within a country depends on who shared data. Simulation uses: rural water supply asset and functionality inventories for planning rehabilitation and new construction, and drought resilience of rural supply. Related records: the WHO/UNICEF JMP database (data-who-unicef-jmp-wash-database) and national water point inventories on HDX (data-hdx-national-water-point-inventories).
